title: Five selected HD 1461 residual waves give no joint HIRES transfer detection in a 2 to 100 day search
abstract: We search 245 HARPS nights for additional HD 1461 velocity waves after two known signals. We select five separated residual peaks from 2 to 100 days and test their fixed phase and amplitude in 215 independent HIRES nights. Waves near 60.6 and 72.6 days each reduce HIRES error by about 3 percent. The best joint null tail fraction is 0.099 to 0.154 with 10-, 30- and 90-day sign blocks. No selected wave passes the joint test at 0.05. Local refinement gives a 365.64-day beat for the two positive peaks, which raises an annual alias concern. A cubic baseline and an alternate HARPS reduction give no joint detection. This is a conditional archive test, not a new planet claim or an exclusion limit. Shared stellar noise, fixed training waves, assumed noise scales and unknown detection power limit the result. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps are included. External database records are excluded.

display.caption: HARPS-only residual scan and fixed-wave error changes in independent HIRES exposures.
